name: background-harness
description: Shared background harness and project context

spec.why: Connect the existing local SDD workflow to a background web runtime with project enrollment and Codex, Claude Code and pi adapters on Linux, macOS and Windows.

requirements.text: Provide an installable runtime with bundled web/harness assets on Linux, macOS and native Windows; installation works outside the source checkout.
treadle start serve starts or reuses one background service per OS user; treadle stop serve stops that verified service and leaves project enrollment intact.

Successful project harness installation enrolls its explicit workspace after ensuring the service; host startup/resume and pre-prompt events reconnect it. After stop, restart occurs on the next relevant event; closing a session leaves the service running.
Persist project identities and trusted real workspace/wiki/spec roots independently of sessions; provide honest connection status, retry, disconnect and missing-root states.
One local web app lists enrolled projects and provides project-qualified existing spec workflow plus read-only wiki navigation/search without slug collisions or cross-project access.
New/continuing-spec agent context reads canonical pack gates, revision, doing task and knowledge references without task admission, mutation or guessing among multiple open packs.
Generate versioned native Claude, supported Codex and pi artifacts from the authoritative harness tree, retaining explicit compatibility installation where native support is absent.

Adapters use verified host lifecycle/output contracts and current event workspace; report runtime, activation/trust and enrollment readiness separately, preserving foreign configuration and avoiding duplicate hooks.
Preserve owner answers, decision acceptance, exact-plan start, sequential task evidence, independent PACK review and separate human Finish; context and adapters perform no owner acts.
Verify the connection and SDD journey across the three operating systems and supported host surfaces; record actual commands/versions/results and keep unsupported or unrun combinations explicit.

out_of_scope: Browser spec-authoring wizard or new approval state machine
Native registry publication and license choice

stories.as: a PO, Dev Lead, developer or QA using the same local session
stories.want: the harness to connect the workspace and restore the correct knowledge/spec context across supported agents
stories.so: we can use the existing owner-gated SDD loop without managing server processes manually

constraints.text: Local single-machine use, with PO, Dev Lead, Dev and QA sharing one agent session; no remote authentication, role permissions or concurrent task-execution leases.

Both new listeners bind 127.0.0.1. Browser UI cannot enroll roots or control the service; privileged control rejects browser origins and requires a private local credential plus exact Host validation.
Runtime state stores project pointers and service identity only; no sessions, prompts, transcripts, credentials in context, telemetry or token usage.
Canonical specs/ wins even when empty; legacy-only external roots remain compatible; archive and .okf are excluded. Core writer lock, held revision and owner receipts remain authoritative.
No native package publication or license decision in this plan; generate/build/install local artifacts for review. Preserve Copilot existing behavior but do not promise new service integration.

design.approach: Add lifecycle, enrollment and read-only context around existing knowledge/workflow; generate host-native packages from one authority.

decisions.decision: One shared per-user background Node runtime, separate from agent lifetimes, with next-event restart and a stable reported UI address.
decisions.because: Avoid duplicate project servers and keep explicit stop effective while sessions are idle.

decisions.decision: Reuse the existing spec engine and owner UI; add project selection and read-only knowledge access. New packs are authored by the agent/CLI into specs/.
decisions.because: The owner workflow already exists; a web spec-authoring wizard and new role system would expand the task.

decisions.decision: Separate credentialed control HTTP from browser HTTP; sandbox Markdown previews on an opaque origin with scripts/forms/top-navigation disabled.
decisions.because: Enrollment expands filesystem reach and trusted Markdown must not acquire control-plane or owner-action authority.

decisions.decision: Generate host-native packages from a versioned harness source manifest; bootstrap and fallback installation remain explicit.
decisions.because: Native hosts should manage activation/versioning while treadle owns its runtime and project enrollment.

decisions.decision: Publish a capability matrix and prove adapters in real hosts, including Codex CLI/desktop separately and IDE compatibility configuration.
decisions.because: Current Codex plugin support excludes IDE; pi package metadata does not promise custom-agent installation. Trust/reload are user host actions.

tasks.title: Implement shared start, stop and status
tasks.detail: Add start serve, stop serve and status serve. Use detached process with disconnected stdio/unref, private per-user state, instance nonce and authenticated health/shutdown. Serialize startup and bound retries; lock recovery requires proof, not age. Fixed preferred UI port may safely choose another and report it; hooks read the descriptor, never assume a port.

tasks.title: Repair installer truth and bootstrap enrollment
tasks.detail: Separate runtime installed, host artifacts wired/activated/trusted, and project connected readiness. Successful project bootstrap ensures then enrolls; awaiting host trust stays visible. Server failure leaves truthful installed-but-disconnected state. Native install without runtime diagnoses bootstrap. Migrate only recorded owned files/wiring; global install needs existing authorization flags and an explicit project connect; --no-hooks does not promise automatic reconnect.
